===============================================================================
RESIDENTIAL DWELLING INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
===============================================================================

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with
the Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated
in the Schedule. Only the peril groups recorded in the Schedule are insured.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

Combined residential buildings insurance protects the policyholder against the
financial consequences of physical damage to their building. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - fire, escape of
water, storm and hail, and further natural hazards among them. Which of the
insurable perils are actually covered is agreed between insurer and policyholder
and recorded in the schedule. A peril group that is not recorded there is not
insured, and damage falling within it is borne by the policyholder.

Where insured property is destroyed or damaged by a peril that is insured, the
insurer indemnifies the cost of putting it back in the same kind and quality. The
technical plant that serves the building, and the electrical installation
belonging to it, share in that cover. A range of consequential expenses triggered
by such a loss event - the removal of what the event destroyed, and the measures
taken to limit the damage among them - is also carried.

The cover is a cover against causes, not against outlay. Every benefit under this
contract presupposes that damage to insured property was caused by an insured
peril and that this has been established.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - an event by which insured property was destroyed or damaged and
which falls within a peril recorded as insured in the schedule.

Established cause - the attribution of the damage to an insured peril, made by
the loss investigation and resting on the identification of the installation, the
defect or the occurrence from which the damage proceeded.

Condition, as distinguished from cause - the state in which the insured property
is found after an event: that a room, a basement, a plant room or a storey stands
or has stood under water, that installations situated there have been submerged,
or that parts of the building are wet. A condition of this kind is the result
that several different perils can produce, some insured and some not. Recording
the condition does not establish a cause, and no benefit under this contract
follows from the condition alone.

Inundation - the standing of water in or on parts of the building or of the
insured site that did not emerge from an installation of the building within the
meaning of 2.4.2. It is immaterial how the water reached the place where it was
found, whether from the ground, from the surface, from precipitation, from a
backing-up, from adjoining land, or from a source that was not identified.

Affected part - a room, a surface, a building component, an installation or an
item in which physical damage caused by an insured event has been established by
the loss investigation.

Repair cost - outlay that serves to put an affected part back into the condition
it was in immediately before an insured event. Outlay that serves another purpose
is not a repair cost, whatever heading it is invoiced under.

Plant of the building - the installations permanently connected to the building
that serve its supply, its heating, its ventilation, its water or its power and
remain in place once the work is finished. Plant of the building is insured
property against the perils recorded in the schedule, and against those only.

Working equipment - the devices, appliances, machines, pumps and comparable items
brought to the insured site in order to carry out an operation and taken away
again once it is finished. Working equipment does not become part of the building
and is not insured property.

Measure - an operation billed by reference to what it achieves rather than by
reference to the items used to achieve it. The removal of standing water is an
example.

Journey charge - a charge for attending the insured site, however described,
including travel, vehicle, company vehicle, call-out, attendance and
re-attendance charges.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage, an item of property or a type of outlay
for which no cover exists.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before, during
and after an insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is destroyed or damaged by, or lost
as a consequence of, the following events, insofar as the group in question is
recorded as insured in the schedule:

  (a) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot.

  (b) ESCAPE OF WATER.

  (c) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (c1) storm and hail;
        (c2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the three groups (a), (b) and (c1) can be taken separately. The further
natural hazards under (c2) can only be taken in combination with one or more of
the perils in (a), (b) or (c1); they are not available on a standalone basis.

Where the schedule does not record group (c2), damage caused by any of the
further natural hazards is not covered, and no part of such damage is brought
into cover by the fact that other groups are recorded.

2.4 Escape of water defined

2.4.2 Escape of water damage
Escaping water means water that has emerged contrary to its intended purpose
from:
  (a) pipes of the water supply, whether supply or drainage lines, or hoses
      connected to them;
  (b) other installations connected to those pipes or hoses, or the
      water-carrying parts of such installations;
  (c) heating or air-conditioning systems;
  (d) water-based extinguishing or sprinkler systems;
  (e) water beds or aquaria.

Operating fluids from heating or air-conditioning systems, and steam, also count
as escaping water. Fluids intended for the generation of energy do not.

2.4.3 What the peril requires
This peril presupposes both of the following:
  (a) that the water proceeded from one of the sources in 2.4.2; and
  (b) that this has been established as a cause within the meaning of 1.3, by
      identification of the installation concerned and of the defect or the
      occurrence by which the water left it.

The presence of water in a room, a basement, a plant room or another part of the
building is the condition that this peril can produce; it is not the peril. It is
equally the condition that inundation produces, and inundation is not this peril.
Where the loss investigation records the condition without establishing which of
the two produced it, the requirements of this clause are not met.

2.4.4 Where the requirements are not met
Where 2.4.3 is not satisfied, the damage is not damage by escape of water. It
falls to be considered under the natural hazards in 2.5, and is covered only
insofar as the schedule records the group into which it falls.

2.5 Natural hazards defined

Storm, hail and the further natural hazards are each defined as customarily in
these conditions. Flood means the inundation of the ground and soil of the
insured site, or of parts of the building, with substantial quantities of surface
water, whether from the overflow of surface waters, from precipitation, or from
the emergence of groundwater at the surface. Backing-up is present where water
enters the building from the building's own drainage pipes or from installations
connected to them.

Inundation within the meaning of 1.3 falls within the further natural hazards
under 2.1(c2) and is insured only where that group is recorded in the schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing
causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered. This applies irrespective
of any contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered. This applies irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.3 Exclusions within the escape of water peril

Damage caused by the following is not covered, irrespective of any contributing
causes except where such causes are named below:
  (a) splash water or cleaning water;
  (b) dry rot and house-rot fungi of every kind;
  (c) groundwater, standing or flowing surface water, flood, precipitation, or a
      backing-up of water brought about by any of these causes;
  (d) earthquake, snow load, avalanche, volcanic eruption;
  (e) ground subsidence or landslip - unless escaping water within the meaning of
      2.4.2 caused the subsidence or the landslip;
  (f) the perils of the fire group;
  (g) storm, hail.

Damage to buildings or parts of buildings that are not ready for occupation is
not covered.

3.6 Inundation, and damage whose cause is not established

3.6.1 The bar
No indemnity arises where the damage was caused by inundation within the meaning
of 1.3 and the schedule does not record the group into which inundation falls,
nor where the loss investigation records only the condition within the meaning of
1.3 without establishing a cause.

3.6.2 The bar applies to the whole claim
The bar in 3.6.1 operates on the claim as a whole and not on individual
positions. Where it applies, the following are not indemnified, whatever they
consist of, whichever trade renders them, and however they are described or
invoiced:
  (a) the repair, renewal or replacement of any installation, component,
      circuit, surface or item, including the plant of the building and the
      electrical installation, and including the adaptation, connection and
      commissioning work belonging to a replacement;
  (b) the labour of any trade, including the labour of examining, testing or
      tracing what has been affected;
  (c) the materials supplied and built in, whether itemised individually or
      billed as a materials position;
  (d) the measures taken, including those taken to remove standing water, to stop
      the spread of water, or to prevent further damage, together with the
      working equipment used for them, however that equipment is charged;
  (e) the clearance, dismantling, removal and disposal of anything taken out,
      whether it was taken out because of the damage or in the course of the
      work;
  (f) every journey charge, of every trade, on every invoice;
  (g) every head of cost under Part 5, and the loss of rent or rental value.

3.6.3 Why the bar reaches the ancillary heads
The costs under Part 5 and the ancillary charges under Part 7 are accessory to an
indemnifiable damage to insured property. They have no existence independent of
it. That work was genuinely carried out, that it was competently done, that it
was reasonable, necessary or urgent, and that it plainly relieved the
policyholder's situation are therefore not grounds on which any part of such a
claim is indemnified.

3.6.4 Burden and effect
It is for the policyholder to establish the cause. Where the cause is not
established, the position is the same as where an uninsured peril is established:
no benefit is payable, and no deductible falls to be applied, since no indemnity
arises from which it could be deducted.

3.6.5 What the bar does not do
The bar concerns this claim only. It does not affect the cover for later events,
does not of itself entitle the insurer to terminate the contract, and does not
prevent the policyholder from bringing forward, within the ordinary limitation
period, evidence establishing a cause within the meaning of 1.3. Where such
evidence is brought forward and accepted, the claim is assessed on its merits
under Parts 5 and 7.

3.7 Work beyond the affected parts, and outlay that is not a repair cost

Work carried out beyond those parts of the insured property that were themselves
affected by an insured event is not covered. Outlay that does not constitute a
repair cost is not indemnified. The delimitation in each case is governed by
7.1.5 to 7.1.9.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises:
  (a) the buildings identified in the schedule;
  (b) their building components;
  (c) their building accessories;
  (d) terraces on the insured site that directly adjoin the building;
  (e) further site installations.

Property is insured against the perils recorded in the schedule and against those
only. That an item is insured property says nothing about whether the peril that
damaged it is covered.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 Building and dwelling
Buildings are structures connected to the ground. They must be capable of
affording protection against external influences and, for the purposes of these
conditions, must be intended for predominantly residential use.

4.2.2 Building components
Building components are items incorporated into a building that have lost their
independence through their firm connection with it. The plant of the building
within the meaning of 1.3 counts as a building component, together with the
pipework, cabling, connection and discharge elements by which it is joined to the
building.

4.2.3 Building accessories
Building accessories are movable items located inside the building or attached to
its exterior that serve the upkeep of the insured building or its predominant
intended purpose.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) photovoltaic installations and their components;
  (b) all items subsequently incorporated into the building by a tenant or by a
      condominium owner where that person both procured or took the items over at
      their own expense and bears the risk for them;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs;
  (d) working equipment within the meaning of 1.3, irrespective of who brings it
      to the insured site, of how it is charged, and of whether it is hired or
      purchased for the occasion.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the insured site: the land parcel on which the insured
building stands, together with the building and its ancillary and technical
rooms.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity that the policyholder bears itself per
insured event. It is deducted once from the indemnity, irrespective of how many
trades, invoices or heads of claim are involved. Where no indemnity arises, no
deductible is applied.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS, LOSS OF RENT AND RENTAL VALUE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

Where damage has been caused by an insured peril and a cause within the meaning
of 1.3 has been established, the insurer reimburses the following costs, insofar
as they were necessary as a consequence of the insured event and were actually
incurred:
  (a) debris removal, dismantling and disposal costs;
  (b) costs of emergency and loss-mitigation measures;
  (c) costs of moving and protecting property;
  (d) costs of accommodating the occupants;
  (e) costs of lost water, gas and heating oil, and of electricity lost from
      storage installations.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it. The
whole of this Part is subject to 3.6.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Debris removal, dismantling and disposal
Costs incurred in clearing away and demolishing insured property, in removing the
remains of that property, transporting them to the nearest disposal site,
depositing them and destroying them. Plant and installations that an insured
event has rendered unusable fall under this head, together with the work of
disconnecting and taking them out.

5.2.2 Emergency and loss-mitigation measures
Costs of the measures reasonably taken to stop the ingress or spread of water, to
remove standing water from rooms, voids and shafts, and to prevent further
damage. Such a measure is indemnified by reference to what it achieves.

The charge for a measure is taken to cover everything deployed in order to
achieve it, including the labour and the working equipment used. Working
equipment is not separately indemnified alongside the charge for the measure it
served, however it is described, whether it is charged as a hire, a deployment, a
supply or a procurement, whether one item or several are charged, and whether the
contractor already owned it or obtained it for the occasion.

5.2.3 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting other property, reimbursable
where those measures serve to reinstate or replace insured property.

5.2.4 Accommodation of the occupants
Costs of accommodation in a hotel or similar, excluding incidentals, where a
dwelling of the insured building cannot reasonably be used because the rooms
themselves are damaged, or because a supply, an installation or a technical room
serving the dwelling has been put out of service by the insured event.

5.3 Loss of rent and rental value

The insurer reimburses loss of rent where tenants of residential premises have
lawfully stopped paying rent in whole or in part on account of an insured event,
and the locally customary rental value of premises occupied by the policyholder
itself where it cannot reasonably be expected to use at least parts of the
dwelling.

5.4 The period for loss of rent and rental value

Loss of rent or rental value is reimbursed for the period during which the rooms
are unusable, but for no longer than [number] months from the occurrence of the
insured event, and only to the extent that the policyholder has not culpably
delayed the resumption of use.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity.

6.2 Index-linked reinstatement value with enhancement

What is insured is the locally customary new-build value of the insured property
identified in the schedule, taken at the time of the insured event, together with
the additional costs arising from public-law restrictions on reinstatement and
the price increases arising between the occurrence of the insured event and
reinstatement initiated without delay.

6.3 Index-linked current value with enhancement where reinstatement is omitted or
    delayed

For property that is not reinstated, or is reinstated late, only the index-linked
current value with enhancement is insured.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the area, the building type, the
construction and the fit-out, the use, the peril groups recorded as insured,
other agreed features material to the premium calculation, and the adjustment
factor. The premium reflects the groups recorded; a group that has not been
rated has not been insured.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted in line with the development of building costs, the
premium changes accordingly, by way of the adjustment factor taking effect from
1 January of each year.

6.7 Subsequent inclusion of a peril group

The policyholder may at any time request that a further peril group be included.
Inclusion takes effect from the date agreed and applies to events occurring after
that date; it does not extend to an event that has already occurred.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 Where damage has been caused by an insured peril and a cause within the
meaning of 1.3 has been established, the insurer reimburses:
  (a) for destroyed buildings - the locally customary reinstatement costs, taken
      at the time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged buildings and other damaged property - the necessary repair
      costs at the time of the insured event, capped at the insurable value at
      that time;
  (c) for destroyed or lost plant of the building and other property - the
      procurement price for property of the same kind and quality in new
      condition, together with the cost of installing it and putting it into
      service.

7.1.5 Extent of the repair
Indemnity is confined to those parts of the insured property that were themselves
affected by the insured event. Work carried out in a room, on a surface, on a
building component, on an installation or on an item that was not itself affected
is not covered, even where it is carried out for reasons of appearance or
convenience, at the same time as covered work, or by the same contractor and
invoiced together with it.

Where the parts of one installation form a functional unit and the unit cannot be
brought back into service by replacing a single part, that unit is the affected
part.

7.1.6 Continuous surfaces
Where only part of a single continuous surface was affected, indemnity extends to
the adjoining unaffected sections of that same surface only where a replacement
material corresponding to the original is no longer obtainable and a visible
discontinuity would otherwise remain.

7.1.7 Preparatory and ancillary work
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) and the replacement costs under
7.1.1(c) include:
  (a) disconnecting, dismantling, taking out and disposing of the affected
      installations, components and finishes;
  (b) the drying, dehumidification and moisture-removal measures necessary before
      the repair can be carried out;
  (c) materials of a type, quality, grade and specification corresponding to
      those in place immediately before the insured event, including the small
      materials, conductors, terminals, fixings and comparable consumable items
      actually built into the covered work;
  (d) where an affected installation cannot economically be repaired and is
      replaced, the work of adapting the immediately adjoining supply, connection
      and discharge elements so far as the replacement requires it, together with
      the work of connecting it and putting it into service;
  (e) the investigatory labour reasonably needed to establish which parts of an
      installation were affected;
  (f) the labour of the workers of each trade necessarily deployed on the covered
      work, at the ordinary rate of that trade;
  (g) one journey charge per insured event, the attendance of the trades being
      treated as one head of cost however many trades attend and however many
      invoices are rendered.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not a repair cost
The following do not constitute repair costs and are not indemnified, however
they may be described or invoiced:
  (a) measures directed at the general condition, cleanliness, upkeep,
      appearance, preservation, modernisation or improvement of the insured
      property, as distinct from making good the damage caused by an insured
      event;
  (b) outlay belonging to a contractor's own business operation rather than to
      the repair - its own tools and consumable small equipment, its diagnostic
      and measuring devices, the provisioning of its personnel, the provision and
      running of its own vehicles and plant, and general administrative,
      handling, processing, coordination or project management charges levied in
      addition to itemised labour and materials. Working equipment within the
      meaning of 1.3 belongs to this heading;
  (c) the same item of cost invoiced more than once in respect of the same
      insured event, whether by one contractor or across several trades;
  (d) every journey charge beyond the first raised in respect of the insured
      event.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
Reinstatement proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade and specification
in place immediately before the insured event. Where a higher specification or a
premium range is chosen instead, indemnity is limited to the cost of an
equivalent standard-grade replacement.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they were
actually incurred, subject to 3.6 and to the limits agreed for each head.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred, and not where the policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim as
to its basis and its amount. Where the insurer determines that no indemnity
arises, it notifies the policyholder in text form, stating the ground and the
clause on which the determination rests.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 Determining the amount of the loss
After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the amount
of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer and
policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly.

8.2 The cause is not determined in this procedure
The procedure determines the amount of the loss. Whether the damage was caused by
an insured peril, and whether a cause within the meaning of 1.3 has been
established, are not determined in it unless the parties expressly agree to
extend it to that question. Where the parties do so agree, the experts are to
state what installation, defect or occurrence the damage proceeded from, or that
this could not be established.

8.3 Procedure before the determination
Each party is to nominate one expert in text form. Before beginning their
determinations, the two experts nominate in text form a third expert as umpire.
Where the experts cannot agree, the umpire is appointed by the court with local
jurisdiction for the loss location.

8.4 Content of the determination
The experts' findings must state a schedule of the destroyed and the damaged
insured property with the corresponding insurable values, the reinstatement and
replacement costs, the residual values, and the insured costs and the insured
loss of rent or rental value.

8.5 Procedure after the determination
The findings of the experts, or of the umpire, are binding on the contracting
parties. They are not binding where it is demonstrated that they manifestly
deviate substantially from the true state of affairs. A determination of the
amount of the loss does not oblige the insurer to pay where no indemnity arises
under Part 3.

8.6 Costs
Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert. The costs of the umpire are borne by the two parties in equal shares.

8.7 Duties remain unaffected
The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Contractually agreed safety requirements before an insured event

9.1.1 Insured property must be kept in proper condition at all times. This
applies in particular to water-carrying installations and equipment. Defects or
damage to such property must be remedied without delay.

9.1.2 Buildings or parts of buildings that are not in use must be inspected
sufficiently frequently at every time of year, and the water-carrying
installations there shut off, drained and kept drained.

9.1.3 During the cold season all buildings and parts of buildings must be heated,
and this must be checked sufficiently frequently.

9.1.4 In rooms at risk of inundation or of backing-up, backflow prevention
devices must be kept operational, the drainage lines on the insured site kept
clear, and installations sensitive to water kept clear of the floor where this is
reasonably possible.

9.2 Duties after an insured event

The policyholder must avert and mitigate the loss so far as it reasonably can,
and must in particular take the measures needed to stop the ingress of water and
to remove standing water without delay. Doing so is required of the policyholder
irrespective of whether the event proves to be covered.

Before the affected parts are altered and before standing water is removed, the
policyholder must so far as reasonably possible record and preserve what shows
where the water came from - the level reached, the direction of ingress, the
condition of the installations present - and must notify the insurer without
delay so that the cause can be established. Where this is not done, the
policyholder bears the consequences of the cause remaining unestablished, in
accordance with 3.6.

9.3 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of the duties in 9.1 or 9.2, the following
applies, subject to the conditions set out in the general contract provisions:
the insurer is entitled to terminate the contract. It may also be wholly or
partly released from liability.

9.4 Circumstances constituting an increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification may exist in particular where a
circumstance changes about which the insurer asked before the contract was
concluded; where the building or the predominant part of it is no longer in use;
where construction work renders it predominantly unusable; or where a commercial
operation is taken up or changed within the building.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION, SECURED LENDERS, TRANSFER OF OWNERSHIP
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation where a security right has been registered

Where a secured lender has registered its charge over the property, cancellation
of the insurance relationship by the policyholder in respect of the fire peril
group is effective only where the policyholder demonstrated, at least one month
before expiry of the insurance contract, that the property was no longer
encumbered with the charge, or that the secured lender consented to the
cancellation. This does not apply to a cancellation following a disposal of the
property, or to a cancellation in the insured event.

10.2 Legal position following a transfer of ownership

Where the policyholder disposes of the insured property, the acquirer steps into
its place in the insurance contract at the date of registration in the land
register, and from that time takes over the rights and obligations of the
policyholder. Seller and acquirer are jointly and severally liable for the
premium for the insurance period in which the transfer of ownership occurs.

10.3 Rights of cancellation on a transfer of ownership

The insurer is entitled to cancel the contract as against the acquirer on one
month's notice, that right lapsing if it is not exercised within one month of the
insurer becoming aware of the disposal. The acquirer is entitled to cancel with
immediate effect or with effect from the end of the current insurance period, in
text form, that right lapsing one month after the acquisition. In either case the
seller alone remains liable for payment of the premium.

10.4 Duties of notification

The disposal must be notified to the insurer without delay, in text form, by the
seller or by the acquirer. Where that notification has been omitted, the insurer
is not obliged to pay in the insured event on the conditions set out in the
general contract provisions.

===============================================================================
END OF DOCUMENT
===============================================================================
case.description:
Heavy rainfall over a short spell caused surface flooding that got into the basement, leaving roughly a meter of water standing in the plant room down there. This was rainwater coming in from outside, not anything to do with the plumbing - the pipes themselves were sound.

The boiler in the basement, along with its flue and storage tank, sat submerged and stopped working, so the whole unit had to be renewed rather than repaired. The old one was hauled out and disposed of, and the supply pipework was adjusted to suit the replacement.

Getting the water out took a fair bit of pumping, so a submersible pump was brought in specifically for it. Once the water was down, an electrician spent the better part of a day and a half on site checking and rewiring the circuits that had been under water.
